changes: No substantive changes. Jīvacandra stays the scribe (svahastena), with the title daivajña (written 'devajña'). NS 412 + 880 = 1292 CE is correct. I expanded the notes on 'śrīmanta' and 'bhāṣā'.

notes: 'devajña' stands for daivajña. 'śrīmanta-' is taken as the honorific śrīmant- in compound with the name (śrīmant + Jīvacandra), not as part of the name; this matches the catalogue's 'Jīvacandra'. The era is not written but is taken as NS: this is a Newari-script manuscript and the catalogue also reads [NS] 412. The word 'bhāṣā' after the year is unclear. It may be the start of a month name or of a vernacular note that was cut off, or something left incomplete by the cataloguer. It cannot be read as any date element. Two stock verses come before the scribal line: 'padmāni bodhayaty arkaḥ…' and the 'udakānalacaurebhyo…' protection verse.
